item.title: Bumrah returns to nets, tests Sooryavanshi with probing deliveries
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Jasprit Bumrah returned to India’s nets at the Kotla and tested teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi with a series of probing deliveries. The pacer’s return brought fresh energy to the camp as Sooryavanshi faced Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh and Yash Thakur
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: There is a different vibe to the Indian team the moment one gentleman checks in.

Jasprit Bumrah was back at the Kotla, all smiles, with a spring in his step and displaying his wide array of skills that kept 15-year-old sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi on his toes.

The last time Sooryavanshi received his maiden call-up, Bumrah was not part of the T20 set-up in the UK and joined the team for the ODIs.

Under the Kotla lights, India’s greatest-ever paceman decided to ask a few probing questions of a Gen Alpha superstar in the making.

The first delivery pitched on a good length and, as Sooryavanshi jabbed at it, he missed it completely.

The next delivery, at the same length, hurried the youngster as it passed his bat before coming down.

The third was a perfect yorker that Sooryavanshi just about managed to dig out.

The fourth was bowled slightly back of a length, and all the youngster could manage was a healthy nick.

Four deliveries and the master craftsman had given a trailer of what Sooryavanshi might have to face at the highest level from countries with better pace attacks.

There was one delivery from Bumrah that was slightly overpitched, and the Boy Wonder dispatched it through the covers.

It wasn’t one of the best training sessions for Sooryavanshi, who missed at least three aerial catches during fielding drills and played and missed against all the pacers.

Yash Thakur, who had received some rough treatment in the Duleep Trophy semifinals, also beat him, as did Arshdeep Singh with some appreciable seam movement.

But if one man stole the show, it had to be Bumrah. He bowled a few deliveries to skipper Shreyas Iyer, who was beaten for pace both on the inside and outside edges.

The pace was there, so was the swag and that smile of a man secure in his craft and sure of himself.

Jasprit Bumrah is back in the nets, and there was happiness in every nook and corner of the Kotla.

item.title: Yemen displacement surges past 46,000 as clashes intensify
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: More than 46,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since fighting escalated last week, with the number rising rapidly, the IOM said. Families are fleeing again as clashes spread, humanitarian access becomes harder and host communities come under growing strain
item.content:encoded:
Geneva: At least 46,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since fighting escalated last week, and the number is alarmingly rising by the hour, the International Organisation for Migration (IOM) said on Friday.

“Families are being forced to flee for the second or third time in this conflict, with almost nothing left,” IOM Director General Amy Pope said in a press release. “As fighting spreads, reaching people with lifesaving assistance is becoming harder. We urgently need safe, unimpeded access.”

She called on all parties to the conflict to guarantee safe humanitarian access and protect civilians, aid workers and assets on the ground, Xinhua News Agency reported.

The figure covers the West Coast and Taiz governorates and continues to climb. Overnight, large numbers of people were reportedly seen leaving Mokha city with their belongings.

IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) team is working to establish updated figures to inform the humanitarian system and its lifesaving response, though communication with affected areas remains highly challenging due to widespread telecommunications disruptions.

New arrivals are being reported in Lahj and Aden governorates, while reports also indicate that people are moving north towards Ibb. Entire villages are reported to have emptied in Maqbanah, Jabal Habashi and Al Ma’afer as clashes moved closer to populated areas.

The Mokha-Taiz road, a key supply route, has reportedly been cut, and host communities in the region are under growing strain.

Yemen’s conflict began in late 2014 when the Houthis seized Sanaa and much of northern Yemen, prompting the Saudi-led coalition to intervene in 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.

The latest advances mark a major battlefield shift along Yemen’s western coast amid one of the sharpest escalations since a UN-brokered truce in 2022 largely halted major hostilities.

item.title: Hindi important but diversity India’s strength, says TGCHE chief
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: language preservation in India, Hindi promotion in Telangana, linguistic diversity in India, Prof V Balakista Reddy speech, Telangana Council of Higher Education news, Official Language Conference Hyderabad, role of language in national unity, Indian languages and cultural heritage, inclusive education through languages, Directorate of National Service Scheme event
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Telangana Council of Higher Education (TGCHE) Chairman Prof. V Balakista Reddy underscored the importance of language in safeguarding India’s cultural heritage and fostering national unity. Speaking at an Official Language Conference in Hyderabad, he stressed that while Hindi holds significance in official communication, India’s true strength lies in its linguistic diversity, which must be preserved and promoted alongside Hindi.

Hyderabad: Telangana Council of Higher Education Chairman Prof. V Balakista Reddy highlighted the vital role of language in preserving India’s cultural heritage, strengthening national unity and promoting inclusive education.

Participating in a one-day Official Language conference organised by the Directorate of National Service Scheme here on Friday, Prof. Reddy said Hindi has an important place in the country’s official communication framework, while India’s greatest strength lies in its rich linguistic diversity.

The promotion of Hindi, he emphasised, should go hand in hand with the respect, preservation and promotion of all Indian languages.

Prof. Reddy observed that languages are not merely instruments of communication but also carry the knowledge, history, traditions, values and intellectual heritage of communities. Every Indian language contributes to India’s collective identity and knowledge ecosystem, he said.

He encouraged students and youth to learn multiple Indian languages while also developing proficiency in English and other global languages.

Sanskriti Shastri, Youth Officer, Directorate of National Service Scheme, Prof. N. Nagaraju, Vice-Chancellor, English and Foreign Languages University and R. Saida, Regional Director, Hyderabad among others also participated in the event.

item.title: PSPB, RSPB, CAG and AIPSCB enter Hockey India nationals semifinals
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: PSPB, RSPB, CAG and AIPSCB advanced to the semifinals of the Hockey India Senior Men Inter-Department National Championship. AIPSCB edged FCI 4-3 in a shootout after their quarterfinal ended 2-2, while the other three semifinalists won in regulation time
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Petroleum Sports Promotion Board (PSPB), Railway Sports Promotion Board (RSPB), Comptroller & Auditor General of India (CAG) and All India Police Sports Control Board (AIPSCB) reached the semifinals of the 6th Hockey India Senior Men Inter-Department National Championship 2026 on Friday.

The knockout stages got underway with all four quarterfinals completed on Friday, headlined by a dramatic shootout finish between All India Police Sports Control Board and Food Corporation of India.

In the first quarterfinal, Petroleum Sports Promotion Board edged past Sports Authority of India 3-2. Gurjot Singh, Manpreet and Varun Kumar were on target for PSPB, while Sachin Dungdung struck twice for SAI in a losing cause.

In the second quarterfinal, Railway Sports Promotion Board kept a clean sheet to beat Central Board of Direct Taxes 2-0, with Singh Gursahibjit and Simranjot Singh finding the net either side of half-time.

In the third quarterfinal, Comptroller & Auditor General of India came through a seven-goal contest against Punjab National Bank, winning 4-3. Skipper Parmod, Majji Ganesh, Deepak and Angad Bir Singh found the target for CAG, while Panchal Prikshit, Abhimanyu and Neeraj replied for Punjab National Bank.

The day’s standout tie was the fourth quarterfinal, in which All India Police Sports Control Board (AIPSCB) and Food Corporation of India could not be separated after regulation time, finishing 2-2. Mohammad Haris and Shamsher Singh scored for AIPSCB, while Navraj Singh struck twice for FCI to force a shootout.

AIPSCB held its nerve from the spot, with Shamsher Singh, Lalit Kumar Upadhyay, Vijay Kumar Gond and Mohammed Haris all finding the target, while goalkeeper Malhotra Paras produced the key saves to seal a 4-3 shootout win and send his side through.

With all four quarterfinals decided, the semifinal line-up is confirmed for September 13. Petroleum Sports Promotion Board will take on Railway Sports Promotion Board in the first semifinal, while Comptroller & Auditor General of India will face All India Police Sports Control Board in the second.

Semifinal line-up:

Semifinal 1: Petroleum Sports Promotion Board vs Railway Sports Promotion Board

Semifinal 2: Comptroller & Auditor General of India vs All India Police Sports Control Board

item.title: HMWSSB drafts roadmap to stop sewage inflow into Durgam Cheruvu
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The HMWSSB is preparing a roadmap to prevent sewage from entering Durgam Cheruvu. Managing Director Ashok Reddy inspected drains, treatment plants and diversion systems, and directed officials to map inflows and survey private STPs in the catchment.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) is preparing a roadmap to prevent sewage from entering Durgam Cheruvu, particularly through nalas during non-rainy periods.

HMWSSB Managing Director Ashok Reddy on Friday inspected nalas entering the lake, sewage flows, sewage treatment plants (STPs), stormwater drains and sewage diversion systems and directed officials to determine the quantities of sewage, treated water and rainwater entering the lake through each route and prepare a comprehensive flow map.

According to a press release, a long-term plan will consider current requirements and the projected increase in sewage volumes by 2047. Ashok Reddy also ordered a comprehensive survey of private STPs at hotels, commercial complexes, high-rise buildings and residential complexes in the lake’s catchment.

He directed officials to expedite ongoing desilting, pipeline connectivity and sewage diversion works. They were also asked to examine an alternative diversion system to prevent sewage from flowing back towards colonies when an STP was not functioning, or inlet routes were blocked.

item.title: Loyola Academy inaugurates new AICUF, MAGIC Youth committees
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Loyola Academy Degree & PG College inaugurated its new AICUF and MAGIC Youth committees under the theme “Torchbearers of Today”. The ceremony highlighted leadership, discipline, responsibility and service, with badges presented to committee members during the Badging Ceremony at Inigo Hall
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Loyola Academy Degree & PG College inaugurated the new committees of AICUF and MAGIC Youth with the theme “Torchbearers of Today” at Inigo Hall on September 9, 2026.

The inaugural ceremony brought together the management, faculty members, coordinators, student leaders, committee members, parents and students to mark the beginning of a new year of leadership and service.

The programme was graced by Rev. Fr. Dr. N. B. Babu, SJ, Principal; Rev. Fr. Dr. A. Rex Angelo, SJ, Correspondent; Rev. Fr. Dr. A. M. Joseph Kumar, SJ, Vice Principal; and Rev. Fr. B. Peter, SJ, Vice Principal and in-charge of the AICUF and MAGIC Youth committees, along with faculty members, parents and students.

Addressing the gathering, Rev. Fr. Dr. A. Rex Angelo emphasised the importance of developing a service-oriented outlook and encouraged members of AICUF and MAGIC Youth to actively participate in their initiatives, contribute meaningfully to the college community and inspire their peers.

Rev. Fr. Dr. N. B. Babu, SJ, Principal, described the occasion as a Day of Commitment, highlighting discipline, responsibility and dedication as essential qualities of student leadership.

The highlight of the ceremony was the Badging Ceremony, during which badges were presented to all members of the AICUF and MAGIC Youth committees

item.title: ‘Anaganaga’ opens in Jubilee Hills with focus on Telugu cuisine
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Anaganaga – Telugu Culinary Tales, a 200-cover speciality restaurant, has opened in Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad. The restaurant showcases traditional Telugu recipes, regional ingredients and contemporary interpretations, while its promoters plan further expansion across key cities through partnership and franchise models.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: ‘Anaganaga – Telugu Culinary Tales’, a 200-cover premium Telugu speciality restaurant, has been launched here on Road No 45, Jubilee Hills, with plans to open three more Anaganaga restaurants across key cities in the coming financial year.

‘Anaganaga – Telugu Culinary Tales’ is spread across two floors and interiors that have subtle references to Telugu art, craft and culture. Its menu brings together traditional recipes, lesser-known preparations, regional ingredients and new interpretations, and the culinary programme is led by corporate chef DVS Pavan Kumar.

Anaganaga is part of the Onamaalu initiative, founded by F&B entrepreneurs Rohith Vasireddy and Gopichand Cherukuri and their partners Vinay Reddy, G Krishna Chaitanya, GVS Sudheer and S Anil, with a larger vision of preserving and celebrating Telugu culinary heritage while creating new expressions of its food, stories and culture.

“We plan to widen Anaganaga’s footprint through both partnership and franchise models. Agreements for Visakhapatnam and Bengaluru are currently in the final stages,” says Rohith. “Over the last three years, we have shaped that idea through research, travel, conversations, and a deeper exploration of Telugu culinary traditions,” says Gopichand.
